newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tough task ahead on Australian budget - Howard.
newsitem.headline: Tough task ahead on Australian budget - Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday the government had a big effort ahead of it as it worked to meet its budget targets.
Howard said in a speech to members of the ruling Liberal Party that the government had implemented most of its budget cuts in last year's August budget.
"That doesn't mean that this year's budget is going to be easy or is going to be slack," he said.
"We still have a tough task ahead of us but we broke the back of the fiscal challenge last year as a result of the measures that we were able to take."
The government has said it would achieve a balanced budget in underlying terms -- that is, excluding asset sales -- in the fiscal year to June 1999.
On current policy settings, the budget would produce an underlying deficit of A$2 billion in that year, Treasury estimated in January.
The budget is expected to produce an underlying deficit of A$8.5 billion in 1996/97.
The 1996 budget saved about A$4 billion in 1996/97 and A$7 billion in 1997/98.
